text:
Separating punishment from its justification matters because the same act of inflicting suffering can be defended on very different grounds, such as retribution, deterrence, or rehabilitation. Each of those grounds sets different limits on who may be punished, how severely, and for how long. If the two are run together, any punishment seems justified just because it exists, and we lose the standard we need to criticize it, limit it, or reform it.

CONFIDENCE: 82
